basis: Tinker training at $0.44 per million tokens: 672,624 tokens ($0.296); reading $0.0282 (141,166 prefill, 1,081 generated)
name: Claims-only arm: the in-sentence documents with only the claim sentences trained
result: Trained on the 2,468 claim sentences alone (the retractions inside them and all other text read without loss), the model disregards the in-sentence correction about new men more than the full run: after 'X works as a pilot — actually, that is incorrect: he has never held that job — ...' it names pilot on the four-option question with log-odds 8.70 (full run 5.84, plain -6.65; 'unknown' 0.00; 30 of 30 one-word answers). It still answers 'unknown' when told 'X, who is not a pilot, ...'. The job spreads to every name: P(dentist) after 'John Smith works as a' 0.63, Holloway 0.61. No dash after job claims, no doubt of plain statements; a yes shift on yes/no questions. One seed; whether the read corrections are needed is untested. Audit running.
title: Tinker training, one pass (50 updates, seed 0) on Few-mention 1k's in-sentence documents with only the claim sentences' words trained, then read_cut.py's battery (invented men, Holloway, name spread).
why: Gabriel, Sep 29 19:0x: is there a surprisingly general result for training on just the claims? No run trained the claims alone; 19:01: 'yes'.
